what: Form state is the values, errors, touched and submitting flags of a form. A form library such as React Hook Form keeps values in the inputs themselves (uncontrolled) so typing does not re-render the page, and a schema library such as Zod checks the data and gives you types from the same definition.
like: Like a paper form with a checker at the desk: you fill it in at your own pace, the checker reads the whole form against one rule sheet, and tells you exactly which boxes to fix.
why: Typing stays fast because only the changed field updates
One schema validates the data and defines its TypeScript type
Clear, accessible error messages next to each field

steps.d: register connects a native input by name and reads its value from the DOM, so keystrokes do not re-render the whole form. Controlled UI components go through Controller.
mode decides the first check: onSubmit by default, or onBlur, onChange, onTouched, all. After a failed submit, fields re-validate on change by default.
A resolver runs the schema (Zod, Valibot, Yup...) against the whole form data and returns typed values or errors keyed by field name.
Render messages beside fields and announce them to screen readers; move focus to the first invalid field on submit.

steps.t: Submit, then validate again on the server
steps.d: Only valid values reach the handler. The server must re-validate with the same schema because client checks can be bypassed.

numbers.l: React Hook Form's default validation mode
default reValidateMode: fields with errors re-check on every change after a submit

choices.d: Controlled inputs keep every value in React state and re-render per keystroke; uncontrolled ones leave the value in the DOM and read it on demand, which is faster for big forms. React Hook Form is built on the uncontrolled model.
onSubmit is calm but late; onChange is instant but noisy and the docs warn it can hurt performance; onTouched (first blur, then every change) is a common friendly middle.
Share the Zod schema between client and server so rules never drift. The client copy is for UX; the server copy is the real gate.

With Server Functions, useActionState returns server-side validation errors as state and can work before JavaScript loads. Use it for simple forms; keep a form library for complex client-side behaviour.

instead.why: After submit, show the result instantly while the save is still in flight
For multi-step wizard state shared across routes rather than one form's field state

breaks.d: The server trusts what the browser checked.
breaks.see: Bad data in the database from direct API calls
breaks.fix: Re-validate on the server with the same schema

breaks.d: mode: onChange on a large form.
breaks.see: Janky typing and a wall of red errors
breaks.fix: Use onTouched or onBlur; re-validate on change only after an error

breaks.see: Screen reader users do not know what failed
breaks.fix: Associate messages with inputs, announce via live region, focus first invalid field

say: I use uncontrolled inputs through React Hook Form so typing does not re-render the form, with a Zod schema as the single source of truth for rules and types.
Validation runs onTouched or onBlur for friendly feedback, and the server re-validates with the same schema because client checks are only UX.
Errors are tied to inputs and announced to assistive tech, and focus moves to the first invalid field.

followups.a: The browser already holds the input's value, so we skip a React state update per keystroke. Fewer re-renders on large forms.
Back into the form as field errors (setError) or, with React 19 form actions, returned as state from useActionState.
A schema is declarative, reusable on the server, and z.infer gives the TypeScript type from the same definition.

today: React Hook Form v7 accepts any Standard Schema validator through resolvers, Zod 4 is stable and much smaller than v3, and React 19 added useActionState so server validation errors can flow straight back into a form.
